name: Fraticelli

citations.excerpt: the name given during the 13th, 14th and 15th centuries to a number of religious groups in Italy, differing widely from each other, but all derived more or less directly from the Franciscan movement.
A name given to various heretical sects which appeared in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, principally in Italy .

facts.value: Groups commonly called Fraticelli, or Brethren of the Poor Life, condemned by John XXII in 1317.

citations.excerpt: Similarly, John XXII. , in his bull Sancta Romana et Universalis Ecclesia (28th of December 1317), condemns vaguely those “ profanae multitudinis viri commonly called Fraticelli, or Brethren of the Poor Life

facts.value_before_verify: Several Italian groups derived from the Franciscans, committed to strict poverty, and condemned by John XXII in 1317.

research_notes: A label for several groups, not one body.
